newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says it favours regional summit on war.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says it favours regional summit on war.

text.p: Zaire said on Friday it favoured the holding of a regional summit on its rebel war but reaffirmed its rejection of negotiations with guerrilla leaders.
Government Spokesman Jean-Claude Biebie said after a cabinet meeting that Zaire and African ministers who met in Kinshasa on Wednesday agreed on a formula for dealing with the conflict.
"The two sides agreed on an enlarged regional summit," he said, without naming which countries should attend.

The ministers who met this week were from a contact group of South Africa, Kenya, Tanzania and Zimbabwe. Two previous summits involving eight countries have been held in Kenya since Tutsi-led rebels took up arms in eastern Zaire last October.
But Biebie said Zaire told the ministers that such regional talks would have better chance of success "after the withdrawal of foreign troops from Zairean territory".
He again ruled out negotiations with rebel leader Laurent Kabila, saying that would amount to "according him a status he does not really have".
"Calls for negotiation in the present context aim, above all, to transform the war of invasion against our country into a civil war," he added.
The statement was issued as South Africa made efforts to shepherd Zaire's warring parties towards peace talks. Sources close to the discussions in Cape Town said progress was slow.

Zaire long ruled out talks with the rebels it accuses of waging a proxy war in its eastern provinces for the neighbouring states of Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi. All three deny involvement in the war, which started in October.
